properties.name: Running a SUBSET of the gate set and reading it as the whole — FOUR times in one day, each time a different subset
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-09-07, on the agent, FOUR TIMES IN ONE SESSION. Recorded as one record with a counted recurrence rather than four, because the instances differ only in which subset was mistaken for the whole.

OCCURRENCE 1 (the original). A new core test called search_design and reindex_search. Run locally it failed with a precise refusal: "this reflow2 was built without the `fulltext` feature, so there is no search index to rebuild". The agent added `--features fulltext` to its own command line, saw green, ran the WORKSPACE suite (which builds with the feature), saw green again, and pushed. CI's core job runs `cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` and failed on all three tests. THE MISREADING, precisely: the refusal was read as a fact about the local command line rather than about a SHIPPED CONFIGURATION — one CI job builds the core without that feature on purpose, to prove it works with no search index and no RocksDB. The flag that made it pass locally is the flag that job does not pass.

OCCURRENCE 2, SAME DAY, ON THE FIX FOR OCCURRENCE 1. Having learned to run both TEST shapes, the agent ran exactly those two and pushed. CI's workspace job also runs CLIPPY, which failed on `explicit_auto_deref` in the helper written that hour. Two test shapes are not the gate set either; the job runs fmt, clippy on both crates, the Python suites and the instruments beside them.

THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL FOUR, and it is the same one three other times today in a different guise: A FIX IS APPLIED WHERE THE PROBLEM WAS SEEN AND THE SAME QUESTION IS NEVER ASKED ONE STEP OVER. The sequence hint fixed in add_epoch and not plan_epoch; the reachability map covering the tools named add_* and not the setters; the test-shape lesson learned for tests and not for lint. Each correction was right where it landed.

THE PROJECT'S OWN MEMORY NAMES IT — A SUBSET OF A GATE SET IS NOT THE GATE SET — with a measurement beside it: `-p reflow2-core` plus `-p reflow2-mcp` run separately is 1778 tests against `--workspace`'s 1824, forty-six short, because a workspace build unifies the rocksdb feature onto core. That note was written for exactly this and was read only after the second failure.

THE HONEST READING, which the memory also states: the only two truthful sentences are "I ran all of it" and "I ran these and not those". Anything in between is this defect.

THE PROPER FIX for occurrence 1 was NOT the obvious one. Gating the whole test file behind the fulltext feature would have made CI green by DELETING coverage from the job with no index. The test was split instead: `claim_age_of` needs no index, so the shared computation runs in every job, and only the assertions that genuinely require a search surface are gated.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the habit has changed. The only evidence will be the next change that runs the whole set before pushing rather than the part that seems relevant.
